rv.q: Their distinct voices are what propel “Entangled” from a traditional tear-jerker into a work of delicate rage.
Charly Evon Simpson and Gabriel Jason Dean break your heart with their seismic words as they interrogate the fallout of mass shootings.
Her Greta is often as funny as she is furious and Naomi Lorrain gives a smashing performance that vibrates with emotional authenticity.
With the entire action consisting of two long, broken monologues, the play isn't consistently gripping.
Amidst its incessant verbosity Entangled contains effective segments particularly as it reaches its wrenching conclusion.
